feature: Native MD event images, visible programme states and 1970 standings

event_images.cause: The previous local pictures filled the entire 217x163 texture. MD uses transparent frame margins with a smaller photograph inset, so an opaque full-size photograph looked displaced and approached the options area.
event_images.credit: Millennium Dawn native country-event frame; individual original artist unknown in this record
event_images.licence_or_permission: Existing MD project material; original upstream rights retained, separate redistribution permission unknown
event_images.photo_credits_and_permissions: Existing individual NASA/JPL/JSC credits and user-supplied illustration records remain authoritative. Unspecified original authors or redistribution permissions remain unknown.
event_images.modifications: Proportional cover crop into the native 180x150 photo inset, with every original frame pixel outside the inset retained. News photographs retain the broad native crop. No recolouring, new illustrative content, provenance captions or visible watermarks added.
event_images.window_audit: The complete country and world-news donors in interface/eventwindow.gui, including picture coordinates, option grid positions and slot width, native option-entry size and title clearance. Shared event window geometry is not modified.

programme_states.source_and_credit: Codex-assisted custom native interface code and procedural colour strips for this project
programme_states.licence_or_permission: User-authorised custom project work; no separate redistribution licence established
programme_states.behaviour: Explicit transparent text overlays show availability, active development, flight, investigation, suspension, qualification, completion and inherited institutions. Status does not rely on a multiline button caption. Restrained six-frame colour strips reinforce the wording. Completed programmes remain reviewable instead of creating page gaps.
programme_states.one_time_programmes: Operational commissioning-only programmes cannot be accepted repeatedly. Suspending operations may require a fresh acceptance to restore operations, but repeat institutional acceptance awards no prestige. Institutions whose full capabilities already exist in the 1970 national profile are marked established, without inventing new mission receipts, research rewards, hardware or upkeep.
programme_states.repeatable_flights: Accepted flight programmes retain their completion record and can fly again only when their real departure requirements are met.

historical_prestige.meaning: Balance values reflecting the situation at the beginning of 1970, not historical statistics or a measured prestige index.
historical_prestige.migration: Once per canonical country tag, including saves already initialised before the change. Adds to existing prestige and never resets earned progress. Does not repeat on startup, GUI access or hotjoin.
historical_prestige.ai: Canonical historical entries can appear even when fewer than three human countries are playing. AI scores remain fixed at their historical baseline; AI countries receive no active Space Race programmes or leadership buffs. Human countries compete using their current baseline plus earned prestige.
historical_prestige.leadership: The unique leading human country receives the existing leadership benefit. Ties, including a tie against a static historical entry, grant no sole-leader benefit.

precedents.claim: Apollo 11 completed a crewed lunar landing and Earth recovery in July 1969, followed by Apollo 12 before 1970.
The Soviet programme had successful lunar orbiters and Zond circumlunar flights before 1970.
Diamant and Asterix established France as the third independent orbital launch power in November 1965.

review_images: Native donor and GUI/font compositions are layout reviews, not live game captures. Embedded source materials retain the credits above.
